ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.claim: The soul mirrors the larger world: God inspires good and evil, inclines it to good and against evil, and requires it to preserve balance; unchecked evil leads to arrogance and disorder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.anchor: inclined it towards good and made it hate evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.claim: The soul itself witnesses its Maker’s purpose: awareness of good and evil entails adopting good and avoiding evil; success is purification and failure is sin, so denying accountability contradicts this witness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.anchor: the awareness of good and evil is found in it. Obviously, the reason for giving him this awareness is that man should adopt good and shield himself from evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r2.claim: Because people can distinguish good from evil, they must choose good and shun evil; this brings success, while vice leads to misery.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r2.anchor: When a person has been given the awareness of good and evil, then it is his obligation to adopt good and shun evil.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r3.claim: The form dassāhā derives from a root meaning to wrap or put something in dirt, with a transformation intensifying the sense of contamination.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r3.anchor: the root which means “to wrap up something in dirt and to put something into dirt.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.claim: Using every divine favour rightly serves one’s own interest and expresses gratitude; failing to do so is self-destruction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.anchor: every favour God has bestowed on him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.claim: As a person who closes his eyes risks falling and bears responsibility, a person must stay alert to the moral path he follows.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.anchor: there is a strong probability that he might fall in a pit and he himself would be responsible for this mishap and no other person.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r6.claim: Some take 91:9–10 as the oath’s complement; Islahi gives weight to al-Zamakhsharī’s rejection of that view.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r6.anchor: there is weight in his rejection.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r2.claim: The purification and corruption statement explains one aspect of the final oath rather than serving as its complement; Islahi endorses al-Zamakhsharī’s view that the complement is suppressed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r2.anchor: a suppression of the muqsam ‘alayh has occurred here.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.claim: Suppressing the complement lets everything evident from the oaths count as its content; one prominent implication is that God destroys rebellious nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.anchor: The benefit of this suppression is that everything

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.claim: Al-Layl develops the preceding sūrah’s claim that the soul succeeds through purification by identifying what corrupts it and how it can be protected and purified.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.anchor: the things which contaminate it are explained

QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r6.claim: The failed soul may be one God has debased, hidden among the righteous despite not belonging to them, or one that a person debased through sin and made contemptible.
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r6.anchor: وقيل : دسها في جملة الصالحين وليس منهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r4.claim: Tadsiyah means concealment; its doubled root is altered by replacing the third doubled consonant with a weak letter, like naqṣu for naqaṣṣa.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r5.claim: Two poetic forms, including a line naming ʿAmr, attest the root d-s-s in the sense of hiding or burying.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر: وأنت الذي دسست عمرا فأصبحت ...

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r2.claim: A person may conceal himself among the good through ostentation while not truly belonging to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r2.anchor: دساها في أهل الخير بالرياء وليس منهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.claim: The mention of taqwā is followed by success for the one who purifies himself, and failure is followed by mention of the people of Paradise as a counterpoint.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.anchor: وحين قال: وتقواها أعقبه بقوله: قد أفلح من زكاها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r4.claim: After describing the failure of the one who debases himself, God names a people as an example from which others should learn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r4.anchor: ولما قال: وقد خاب من دساها، أعقبه بأهل الجنة.

FARRA:v3p266/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p266/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p266/r7.claim: One explanation makes God the subject: the soul He purifies succeeds, and the soul He hides away fails.
FARRA:v3p266/r7.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: قد أفلح من زكاها (9) يقول: قد أفلحت نفس زكاها الله، وقد خابت نفس دساها،

FARRA:v3p266/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p266/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p266/r8.claim: Another explanation makes the person the subject: one succeeds by purifying the soul through obedience and charity and fails by neglecting both.
FARRA:v3p266/r8.anchor: ويقال: قد أفلح من زكى نفسه بالطاعة والصدقة، وقد خاب من دسى نفسه،

FARRA:v3p266/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p266/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p266/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ derives dassāhā from dasastu, with a doubled s assimilated to yāʾ; Arabic similarly shifts doubled letters to yāʾ or wāw, and both explanations are sound.
FARRA:v3p266/r9.anchor: ونرى- والله أعلم- أن دساها من: دسست، بدلت بعض سيناتها ياء، كما قالوا: تظنيت من: الظن،

NAHHAS:v5p235/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r11.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p235/r11.claim: He says the one who succeeds is the one who purifies the soul through righteous action.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة قد أفلح من زكى نفسه بالعمل الصالح

NAHHAS:v5p235/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p235/r12.claim: If God is the subject of purifying, the relative pronoun cannot straightforwardly resume an element of its own clause; possible workarounds treat man as soul or as a group.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r12.anchor: وذلك أنه إذا كان الضمير يعود على الله جل وعز لم يعد على من من صلته شيء إلا على حيلة بعيدة

NAHHAS:v5p235/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p235/r13.claim: God's purification means enabling obedience; zakā for wealth can mean either growth by paying alms or cleansing wealth by giving the poor their share.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r13.anchor: ومعنى زكاها الله طهرها بالتوفيق لطاعته وزكى فلان ماله في اشتقاقه قولان أحدهما أنه من زكا الزرع إذا زاد ونما

NAHHAS:v5p235/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p235/r14.claim: The alternative derivation makes zakā mean purifying and freeing wealth through the poor's share; zakiyya and zakī likewise mean pure.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r14.anchor: والقول الآخر بين حسن يكون زكى ماله

NAHHAS:v5p235/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p235/r15.claim: Khāba means failed to attain the goal; God may have abandoned the soul to sin, or the sinner may have buried it under sin, with yāʾ replacing one of two sīn letters.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r15.anchor: وقد خاب أي لم يظفر بما يريد من دسى نفسه الله أي خذلها فارتكبت المعاصي وعلى القول الآخر من دسى نفسه أي سترها لركوب المعصية فاشتقاقه من دس ودسس فأبدل من أحد السينين ياء

DURR-FULL:v8p527/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r8.claim: He glossed the sun as its light, the moon as following it, daylight as illuminating it, God as builder of heaven, the earth as spread out, inspiration as showing good and evil, and corruption as leading astray.
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {و الشمس وضحاها}

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses suppressing the soul as leading it astray.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r8.anchor: وقد خاب من دساها قال : اغواها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r11.claim: Mujahid says God fashioned the soul's creation without leaving anything out.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد والشمس وضحاها قال اشراقها والقمر اذا تلاها قال : يتلوها والنهار اذا جلاها قال : حين ينجلي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r17.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r17.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r17.claim: Ikrimah says the soul is ruined.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r17.anchor: عن عكرمة من دساها قال : من خسرها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r19.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r19.claim: Ibn Abbas says loss means God lets the soul be suppressed and led astray.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r19.anchor: وقد خاب من دساها يقول : قد خاب من دس الله نفسه فاضله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r21.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r21.claim: Ibn Abbas also says suppression means plotting against the soul.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r21.anchor: عن ابن عباس وقد خاب من دساها يعني : مكر بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.claim: The oath is prepared by noting that purifying the soul leads to success, while neglecting its reform leads to immorality and loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.anchor: ومهد لذلك بالتنبيه على أن تزكية النفس سبب الفلاح ، وأن التقصير في إصلاحها سبب الفجور والخسران .

JISHUMI:v10p7429/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r1.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet says that reciting Sūrat al-Shams is like giving charity to everything reached by the sun and moon.
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r1.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: من قرأ سورة (والشمس وضحاها)

JISHUMI:v10p7429/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r2.claim: The previous chapter describes success through obedience and punishment for corrupting oneself; this chapter calls obedience purification instead of the previous chapter's steep path, with the same meaning.
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r2.anchor: فعبر في هذه السورة عن الطاعات بالتزكية، وفى تلك السورة بالعقبة، والمعنى واحد

JISHUMI:v10p7429/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r3.claim: They pronounce the verse endings with fatḥ and tafkhīm; al-Kisāʾī uses imāla throughout, while other readers use intermediate or root-conditioned patterns.
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم: ضحاها وتلاها وسائر أواخر الآي إلى آخر السورة بالفتح والتفخيم

JISHUMI:v10p7429/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r4.claim: Imāla lightens pronunciation; fatḥ is the original, while an intermediate sound both eases pronunciation and signals the original form.
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r4.anchor: أما الإمالة فللتخفيف، والفتح الأصل، وما بين ذلك للتخفيف والإشعار بالأصل

JISHUMI:v10p7429/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r9.claim: Dassa oneself is the opposite of purifying oneself: corrupt acts bury the self in loss and damage.
JISHUMI:v10p7429/r9.anchor: ودس نفسه نقيض زكاها، كأنه دسها بالعمل الفاسد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.claim: Inspiring vice and piety means making their difference clear and enabling choice; the following verses show the human being performs purification or defilement, which respectively elevate through piety or diminish through sin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.anchor: ومعنى إلهام الفجور والتقوى : إفهامهما وإعقالهما ، وأن أحدهما حسن والآخر قبيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r9.claim: Asked about the words, Ibn Abbas points to ‘successful is the one who purifies himself’ and ‘he has failed who bears wrongdoing.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r9.anchor: أتقرأ : { قد أفلح من تزكى } ، ( الأعلى : 14 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r10.claim: The claim that God is the agent of purifying and defiling is, in the author's view, a distortion by Qadariyya who falsely attribute reprehensible destiny to God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r10.anchor: وأما قول من زعم أن الضمير في زكى ودسى لله تعالى ، وأن تأنيث الراجع إلى من

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r1.claim: A verse attributed to al-Khansa, using دسيت, illustrates the sense of debasing or sullying the soul.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r1.anchor: وأنت الذي دسيت عمرا فأصبحت حلائلهم فيهم أرامل ضيعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r2.claim: Qatada interprets the soul's being debased as its sin and wickedness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r3.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r3.claim: Ikrima glosses the soul's debasement as its loss.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r3.anchor: الثالث : خسرها , قاله عكرمة . الرابع : كذبها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as calling the soul false.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r4.anchor: الرابع : كذبها , قاله ابن عباس . الخامس : أشقاها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r5.speaker: ابن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r5.claim: Ibn Sallam says the soul was made wretched.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r6.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says the phrase means turning the soul away from good.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r6.anchor: السادس : جنبها في الخير , وهذا قول الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r7.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r7.claim: Ibn Isa explains it as hiding and diminishing the soul through miserliness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p284/r7.anchor: السابع : أخفاها وأخملها بالبخل , حكاه ابن عيسى .

STUDYQURAN:91:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:intro/r2.claim: The first ten verses establish physical and spiritual polarity: eight oaths lead to the soul's choice between iniquity and purity, continuing 90:10's two highways and right-left contrast.
STUDYQURAN:91:intro/r2.anchor: The first ten verses emphasize the physical and spiritual polarity inherent in creation

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.claim: An eight-verse oath series leads into the antithetical statement in verses 9–10; the pre-Islamic genre is repurposed in verses 5–7 to express biblical creation ideas.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.anchor: mit anschließender, antithetischer Schwuraussage (V. 9.10). Die Schwurserie

TABRISI:91:1-15/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:1-15/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:91:1-15/r18.claim: To hide the soul is to mislead and destroy it; Qatada glosses the word as making it sinful.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r9.claim: After the oaths, the surah's central message is responsibility: the one who purifies the soul succeeds, while the one who lets it follow evil loses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r9.anchor: 1-8. âyetlerde yer alan yemin ifadelerinden sonra 9-10. âyetlerde sûrenin asıl mesajı olan insanın sorumluluğuna dikkat çekilmiş

BURSEVI:v10p344/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p344/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v10p344/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said purifying the self purifies the heart: when desire is cleansed from the self, the heart is freed from attachment to everything besides God.
BURSEVI:v10p344/r1.anchor: وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ، روايت كرده كه حضرت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v10p344/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p344/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p344/r2.claim: Although God creates and decrees human acts, an act is attributed to its human agent, as one says Zayd struck rather than God struck.
BURSEVI:v10p344/r2.anchor: وكون أفعال العبد بتقدير الله تعالى وخلقه لا ينافي إسناد الفعل إلى العبد

BURSEVI:v10p344/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p344/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p344/r3.claim: Purifying the soul earns praiseworthy traits and reward; purification is attributed to the servant's effort, God as true agent, the means such as charity, or worship as its instrument.
BURSEVI:v10p344/r3.anchor: قال الراغب : وبزكاء النفس وطهارتها يصير الإنسان بحيث يستحق في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p344/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p344/r4.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v10p344/r4.claim: Khaba means to fail, lose, be deprived, or miss one's aim; dassa derives from repeated concealment, with the final doubled consonant assimilated to ي.
BURSEVI:v10p344/r4.anchor: في "القاموس" خاب يخب خيبة حرم وخسر

BURSEVI:v10p344/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p344/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p344/r5.claim: Raghib defines d-s-s as forcing one thing into another; hiding the soul means burying it in sins.
BURSEVI:v10p344/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب : الدس إدخال الشيء في الشيء بضرب من الإكراه

BURSEVI:v10p344/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p344/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p344/r6.claim: The loser diminishes and conceals the soul through sin and unleashes it into natural appetites.
BURSEVI:v10p344/r6.anchor: والمعنى قد خسر من نقصها وأخفاها بالفجور وبإرسالها في المشتهيات الطبيعية

QASHANI:91:9-10/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:91:9-10/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:91:9-10/r2.claim: The failed hide the soul in the body’s soil, away from divine light and mercy.
QASHANI:91:9-10/r2.anchor: وأخفّاها في تراب البدن عن نور الحق ورحمته

QASHANI:91:9-10/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:91:9-10/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:91:9-10/r3.claim: The oath’s omitted answer is that veiled deniers of the Prophet will perish through transgression as Thamud did, because they reject the inspiration, remain sinful, veil intellect, and let the dark self dominate.
QASHANI:91:9-10/r3.anchor: ليّهلكن المحجوبون المكذبون للنبي بطغيانهم كما أهلكت ثمود لتكذيبهم نبيهم بطغيانهم

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r3.claim: Success means examining where one's food comes from; failure is neglecting that.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عثمان المغربي : افلح من نظر من أين مطعمه

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r4.claim: Success protects the inner secret from worldly pollution; failure occupies that secret with the world.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : افلح من طهر ستره عن التدنس بالدنيا

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r5.claim: Success is knowing what God requires and addresses to one; failure is neglecting it.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : افلح من علم ما يراد منه وما يخاطب به

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r7.claim: The successful turn toward their Lord, and the unsuccessful turn away.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أفلح من أقبل على ربه ، وخاب من اعرض عنه

IBNASHUR:91:10/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:10/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:10/r1.claim: Dassa-hā means keeping the soul from doing good; the root means hiding something by putting it under something else.

IBNASHUR:91:10/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:10/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:10/r2.claim: The doubled consonant in dassā was changed to yāʾ for ease, as in the forms taqaḍḍā/taqaḍḍaḍ and tazannaytu.
IBNASHUR:91:10/r2.anchor: فأبدلوا الحرف المضاعف ياء طلباً للتخفيف

IBNASHUR:91:10/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:10/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:10/r3.claim: If purification answers the oath, the account of Thamūd demonstrates the failure expressed here.

IBNASHUR:91:10/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:10/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:10/r4.claim: People seek either lasting benefit and perfection or immediate, false gains that decay into loss; this verse describes the latter as failure in the Hereafter.
IBNASHUR:91:10/r4.anchor: والمقصود هنا الفلاح في الآخرة والخيبة فيها

IBNASHUR:91:10/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:10/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:10/r5.claim: The passage repeatedly uses antithesis: sun/moon, day/night, illumination/covering, heaven/earth, building/spreading, vice/piety, success/failure, and purification/corruption.
IBNASHUR:91:10/r5.anchor: وفي هذه الآيات مُحسّن الطباق غير مرّة فقد ذكرت أشياء متقابلة متضادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r4.claim: The success-and-failure statement may answer the oath, like the answer in Sūrat al-Layl, or interrupt it to explain that the soul succeeds by choosing its divinely indicated piety.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r4.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الجملة جواب القسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.claim: This contrast prepares the lesson of Thamūd: their punishment followed from corrupting their souls through arrogance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.anchor: وهذه الجملة توطئة لجملة : كذبت ثمود بطغواها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r6.claim: The human who purifies the soul and that soul are the same being, presented as two because of choice and action; tazkiyah means increasing goodness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r6.anchor: فالإنسان والنفس شيء واحد ، ونزلا منزلة شيئين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r7.claim: Dassāhā means preventing the soul from good; its root is hiding something beneath another, with consonant substitution for ease as in other Arabic forms.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.claim: If success and failure answer the oath, Thamūd's denial is evidence for the failure of those who corrupt their souls.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.anchor: في موقع الدليل لمضمون جملة { وقد خاب من دساها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r2.claim: Success is attaining one's aim and failure is being deprived of it; lasting good is true success, while transient gain that turns into decline is failure, ultimately in the afterlife.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r3.claim: The passage repeatedly uses antithesis: sun and moon, day and night, disclosure and concealment, heaven and earth, building and spreading, transgression and piety, success and failure, purification and corruption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r3.anchor: وفي هذه الآيات محسن الطباق غير مرة فقد ذكرت أشياء متقابلة متضادة

TUSTARI:91:10/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:91:10/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:91:10/r1.claim: A soul that God lets go astray fails because it does not consider its afterlife.
TUSTARI:91:10/r1.anchor: قال: خسرت نفس أغواها الله عز وجل، فلم تنظر في أمر معاده.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r11.speaker: ثعلب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r11.claim: Tha'lab says a person may conceal his soul by showing off among the righteous without truly belonging to them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r11.anchor: وقال ثعلب معنى الآية وقد خاب من دساها في أهل الخير بالرياء وليس منهم في حقيقته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r1.claim: If God is the subject, He has abandoned and disgraced the soul, concealed it through disbelief and sin, and left it unrecognized for good works.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r1.anchor: فإن قلنا إن الفعل لله فمعنى دساها خذلها وأخملها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r2.claim: If the human is the subject, he hides himself through wickedness; al-Farrāʾ reports dassāhā as dassasahā, like a miser hiding his home and wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r2.anchor: وإن قلنا الفعل للإنسان فمعنى دساها أخفاها بالفجور قال الفراء ويروى أن دساها دسسها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says a sinful person hides himself in vice; the form comes from dassastu, as qaṣṣaytu represents qaṣaṣtu.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة المعنى دسى نفسه أي أخفاها بالفجور والمعصية والأصل من دسست

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r4.claim: By committing indecencies a person buries and suppresses himself; a benefactor makes himself visible and elevated, as generous Arabs lodged on hilltops while ignoble ones hid on the outskirts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r4.anchor: فكأن النطف بارتكاب الفواحش دس نفسه وقمعها ومصطنع المعروف شهر نفسه ورفعها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says dassāhā means making the soul low and base.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141#2/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج معنى دساها جعلها قليلة خسيسة

IBNKATHIR:91:9/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r8.claim: The one who fails has been degraded and kept from guidance until he commits sins and abandons obedience to God.
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r8.anchor: أي : أخملها ووضع منها بخذلانه إياها عن الهُدَى ،   حتى ركب المعاصي وترك طاعة الله عز وجل .

IBNKATHIR:91:9/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r9.claim: A second possible reading, attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas by al-ʿAwfi and ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, is that God purifies the successful soul and debases the failed one.
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r9.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون المعنى : قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه ،   وقد خاب من دَسَّى الله نفسه

IBNKATHIR:91:10/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:10/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:10/r8.claim: The one who fails has been degraded and kept from guidance until he commits sins and abandons obedience to God.
IBNKATHIR:91:10/r8.anchor: أي : أخملها ووضع منها بخذلانه إياها عن الهُدَى ،   حتى ركب المعاصي وترك طاعة الله عز وجل .

IBNKATHIR:91:10/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:10/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:91:10/r9.claim: A second possible reading, attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas by al-ʿAwfi and ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, is that God purifies the successful soul and debases the failed one.
IBNKATHIR:91:10/r9.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون المعنى : قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه ،   وقد خاب من دَسَّى الله نفسه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#2/r1.claim: Dassa means he hid himself through sin and disobedience.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#2/r1.anchor:
{وقد خاب من دساها} أي دس نفسه- أي أخفاها- بالفجور والمعصية.
والأصل

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#2/r2.claim: The form comes from dassastu, with the second sīn turned into yāʾ, as in qaṣaytu for qaṣaṣtu.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#2/r2.anchor: من (1) "دسست" فقلبت السين ياء. كما قالوا: قصيت أظفاري، أي قصصتها.

JISHUMI:v10p7433/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r1.claim: The oath by these things, or by their Creator, marks their great significance as signs of divine power and blessing.
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r1.anchor: يدل القسم بهذه الأشياء على عظم محلها في القدرة والنعمة

JISHUMI:v10p7433/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r2.claim: The inspiration of the soul means God showed every accountable person good and evil and enabled both choices.
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى بين لجميع المكلفين طريق الخير والشر

JISHUMI:v10p7433/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r3.claim: Success comes by avoiding sins and purifying the soul; the pronoun most plausibly refers to the soul just mentioned.
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r3.anchor: والأولى أن تحمل الكناية على النفس

JISHUMI:v10p7433/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7433/r4.claim: Failure comes through sins, and these teachings together encourage and warn.

KASHSHAF:91:9/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:9/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:9/r1.claim: The person acts as agent of purification or debasement; purification grows and elevates through piety, while debasement diminishes and conceals through sin.

KASHSHAF:91:9/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:9/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:9/r2.claim: The root of dassaha is d-s-s, like the form cited for taqadada.
KASHSHAF:91:9/r2.anchor: وأصل دسى : دسس ،   كما قيل في تقضض

KASHSHAF:91:9/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:9/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:9/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects the Qadari view that God is the subject of purification and debasement, condemning their attribution of an evil destiny to God.
KASHSHAF:91:9/r4.anchor: وأما قول من زعم أنّ الضمير في زكّى ودسى لله تعالى

KASHSHAF:91:9/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:9/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:9/r5.claim: The oath's omitted answer is that God will destroy the people of Mecca for denying Muhammad as He destroyed Thamud for denying Salih; the success saying is a tangent from the preceding verse, not the oath's answer.
KASHSHAF:91:9/r5.anchor: هو محذوف تقديره : ليدمدمنّ الله عليهم

KASHSHAF:91:10/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:10/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:10/r1.claim: The person acts as agent of purification or debasement; purification grows and elevates through piety, while debasement diminishes and conceals through sin.

KASHSHAF:91:10/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:10/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:10/r2.claim: The root of dassaha is d-s-s, like the form cited for taqadada.
KASHSHAF:91:10/r2.anchor: وأصل دسى : دسس ،   كما قيل في تقضض

KASHSHAF:91:10/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:10/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:10/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects the Qadari view that God is the subject of purification and debasement, condemning their attribution of an evil destiny to God.
KASHSHAF:91:10/r4.anchor: وأما قول من زعم أنّ الضمير في زكّى ودسى لله تعالى

KASHSHAF:91:10/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:10/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:10/r5.claim: The oath's omitted answer is that God will destroy the people of Mecca for denying Muhammad as He destroyed Thamud for denying Salih; the success saying is a tangent from the preceding verse, not the oath's answer.
KASHSHAF:91:10/r5.anchor: هو محذوف تقديره : ليدمدمنّ الله عليهم

MAJAZ:v2p300/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p300/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p300/r2.claim: Dassanā derives from dassastu; Arabs can turn a doubled consonant into yāʾ, as in al-ʿAjjāj’s cited example.
MAJAZ:v2p300/r2.anchor: «خاب من دساها» (10) هى من دسست والعرب تقلب حروف المضاعف إلى الياء قال العجاج:

MAJAZ:v2p300/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p300/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p300/r3.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s taqaḍḍā al-bāzī exemplifies the consonant change; its underlying form is al-qaḍḍāḍ.
MAJAZ:v2p300/r3.anchor: قال العجاج: تقضى البازي إذا البازي كسر [943] وإنما هو القضاض.

MAJAZ:v2p300/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p300/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p300/r4.claim: Taẓannaytu is a form of taẓannantu, with the doubled consonant altered to yāʾ.
MAJAZ:v2p300/r4.anchor: وتظنيت إنما هو تظننت ورجل ملب وإنما هو من ألببت

MAJAZ:v2p300/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p300/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p300/r5.claim: Mulibb comes from albabtu and means one who has stayed or settled in a place.
MAJAZ:v2p300/r5.anchor: ورجل ملب وإنما هو من ألببت أي قد أقمت بالمكان

MAJAZ:v2p300/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p300/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p300/r6.claim: Al-Muḍarrib ibn Kaʿb’s line uses labīb to mean resident or settled, glossed as ‘staying there.’
MAJAZ:v2p300/r6.anchor: أي قد أقمت بالمكان وقد ألب الرجل قال المضرب بن كعب: فقلت لها فيئي إليك فإننى ... حرام وإنى بعد ذاك لبيب (172) أي مقيم أي مع ذاك.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r26.claim: One reading says a person failed by God's decree in the way He made the soul corrupt; another says the person corrupted his own soul.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r27.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r27.claim: They interpret dassāhā as misleading or leading the soul astray by sinking it into sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r27.anchor: قاله مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير , لأنه دسى نفسه

MUJAHID:v2p763#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p763#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p763#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says the one who failed is the person whom God led astray.
MUJAHID:v2p763#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وقد خاب من دساها ﴾ يعني خاب من أغواه الله عز وجل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#4/r1.speaker: عكرمة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#4/r1.claim: Ikrima says the soul purified by God succeeds and the soul God led astray fails.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#4/r1.anchor: قال عكرمة أفلحت نفس زكاها الله وخابت نفس أغواها الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#4/r2.claim: Alternatively, the human being performs purification and concealment: concealment is reduction and hiding through sin; the root dassa is originally doubled sīn, with yāʾ replacing one.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#4/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون التدسية والتطهير فعل العبدو التدسية والنقص والاخفاء

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r2.claim: Another analysis omits the oath’s answer: “by the sun and so on, you will surely be resurrected.”
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r2.anchor: وقيل: الجواب محذوف أي والشمس وكذا وكذا لتبعثن

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r4.claim: Another view puts the successful/pitiable statements before the oath by inversion, without ellipsis.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو على التقديم والتأخير بغير حذف

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says a soul fails when God leads it astray.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: خابت نفس أضلها وأغواها

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r8.claim: Qatada and others say a person succeeds by purifying himself with obedience and good deeds, and fails by hiding himself in sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r8.anchor: وقيل: أفلح من زكى نفسه بطاعة الله، وصالح الأعمال، وخاب من دس نفسه في المعاصي قاله قتادة وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r10.claim: Generous Arabs settled on high ground and lit fires for visitors; stingy people hid in hollows, just as virtue raises and sin conceals a person.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r10.anchor: فمصطنع المعروف والمبادر إلى أعمال البر، شهر نفسه ورفعها. وكانت أجواد العرب تنزل الربا وارتفاع الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r11.claim: The sinner hides from view, loses manliness, and lowers his head through sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r11.anchor: وكذا الفاجر أبدا خفي المكان، زمر المروءة، غامض الشخص، ناكس الرأس بركوب المعاصي

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r12.claim: Another explanation of dassaha is “led it astray,” illustrated by a poem about Amr’s wives becoming widows.

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r13.speaker: أهل اللغة
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r13.claim: Linguists derive dassaha from dassasaha, insertion by assimilation; the sīn changes to yāʾ as in qadaytu for qasadtu.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r13.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: والأصل: دسسها، من التدسيس

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r14.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r14.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says it means hiding a soul among the righteous although one is not one of them.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r14.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: { وقد خاب من دساها } أي دس نفس في جملة الصالحين

QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r1.claim: Suppressing and weakening the conscious faculty leads to failure.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r1.anchor: ومن أظلم هذه القوة وخبأها وأضعفها فقد خاب

QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r2.claim: Human freedom entails accountability, capacity entails obligation, and divine gift entails duty; choice directs innate capacities toward either good or evil.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r2.anchor: فهي حرية تقابلها تبعة ، وقدرة يقابلها تكليف ، ومنحة يقابلها واجب

QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r3.claim: In mercy, God does not leave people to instinct or unaided will: revelation supplies firm measures, faith-inspiring signs, and guidance in the self and the world, clearing away caprice.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r3.anchor: فأعانه بالرسالات التي تضع له الموازين الثابتة الدقيقة ، وتكشف له عن موحيات الإيمان

QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r4.claim: When the conscious faculty sees the path clearly, it chooses knowingly; whatever occurs within this divinely granted freedom fulfills God's encompassing will and decree.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r4.anchor: فتتصرف القوة الواعية حينئذ عن بصيرة وإدراك لحقيقة الاتجاه الذي تختاره وتسير فيه

QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r5.claim: This view honors humans by making them capable of choice and responsible for its direction, while locating that freedom within God's will.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r5.anchor: فالحرية والتبعة يضعان هذا الكائن في مكان كريم ، ويقرران له في هذا الوجود منزلة عالية

QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r6.claim: People bear responsibility for their fate; God's decree concerning them is realized through their own conduct, which should awaken vigilance and reverent caution.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r6.anchor: وهو يعلم أن قدر الله فيه يتحقق من خلال تصرفه هو بنفسه

QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r7.claim: People continually need God's stable measures to test whether desire has deceived them, and to stay near God through His guidance and light.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r7.anchor: تشعر هذا الإنسان بالحاجة الدائمة للرجوع إلى الموازين الإلهية الثابتة

QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r8.claim: Purification has no endpoint: the person can keep cleansing the self in God's abundant light and the flowing springs of existence.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:10/r8.anchor: فلا نهاية لما يملك هذا الإنسان أن يصل إليه من تزكية النفس وتطهيرها

RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r1.claim: Dassa is derived from tad sīs, concealing one thing in another; the original d-s-s form was altered by replacing one sīn with yāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r1.anchor: فقالوا : { دساها } أصله دسسها من التدسيس

RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r2.claim: The Muʿtazila say the righteous show themselves openly while sinners hide; generous Arabs publicize camps and night fires, unlike misers hiding from people seeking aid.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r2.anchor: أن أهل الصلاح يظهرون أنفسهم ، وأهل الفسق يخفون أنفسهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r3.claim: A second Muʿtazili gloss is that the loser concealed himself among the righteous despite not belonging to them.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r3.anchor: خاب من دساها } أي دس نفسه في جملة الصالحين

RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r4.claim: Another gloss says the loser buried himself in sins until submerged in them.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r4.anchor: من دساها } في المعاصي حتى انغمس فيها

RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r5.claim: Another says a person instills wickedness through persistent sin and keeping sinful company.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r5.anchor: من دس في نفسه الفجور ، وذلك بسبب مواظبته عليها

RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r6.claim: A final gloss says abandoning obedience for sin leaves a person obscure and forgotten, like a thing hidden away.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r6.anchor: أن من أعرض عن الطاعات واشتغل بالمعاصي صار خاملا

RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r7.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r7.claim: Razi's school says a soul fails when God misguides, seduces, makes it wicked, invalidates, and destroys it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r7.anchor: وأما أصحابنا فقالوا : المعنى خابت وخسرت نفس أضلها الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r8.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi says God swears by the noblest creatures to the success of the soul He purifies and the loss of the one He abandons, precluding self-directed purification or ruin outside prior decree.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r8.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : فكأنه سبحانه أقسم بأشرف مخلوقاته

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r1.claim: These verses inspired extensive writing on purification of the soul, regarded by some as the Quran's entire purpose.
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r1.anchor: These two verses have served as the inspiration for extensive literature on the “purification of the soul”

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r3.claim: The verses describe cleansing lowly traits and, conversely, dulling the soul through heedlessness and disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r3.anchor: The text speaks of those who cleanse the soul of lowly and despicable character traits

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r4.speaker: IK, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r4.claim: Some early commentators make God the subject: the soul God purifies prospers, and the soul He obscures fails.
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r4.anchor: According to some of the earliest commentators, these two verses could also be read with God as the subject

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r5.claim: The subject's ambiguity can express cooperation between God and people: people purify themselves for their own souls while willing only as God wills; God purifies whom He will, yet changes a people when they change themselves.
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r5.anchor: The ambiguity of the subject can also be seen as an allusion to the cooperation between God and human beings

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r6.speaker: Sh, Z
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r6.claim: The literal meanings are to grow for purify and to bury for obscure; the verses can be rendered whoever grows the soul prospers, whoever buries it fails.

SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r6.claim: The apparent subject of zakāhā and dassāhā is man; an alternative makes God the subject, but the author rejects it as syntactically awkward because the pronoun must refer back through nafs and its possessor.
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r6.anchor: والحق أنه خلاف الظاهر، لا لما قال الزمخشري، بل لمنافرة نظمه للاحتياج إلى عود الضمير على النفس

SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r1.claim: Dassāhā derives from dassasahā; repeated like consonants led the third s to be replaced by a weak letter, as in qaṣaytu.
SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r1.anchor: أصله دسسها فكثرت الأمثال فأبدل من ثالثها حرف علة كما قالوا: قصيت [أظفاري

SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r2.claim: Tadsiyah means concealment: the soul was hidden through wickedness; the cited poets retain the unreduced root in their use of dassa.
SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r2.anchor: والتدسية: الإخفاء بمعنى أخفاها بالفجور، وقد نطق بالأصل من قال

SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r3.claim: The poet describes having hidden ʿAmr, whose wives were left widowed and abandoned.
SAMIN-DURR:91:10/r3.anchor:
وأنت الذي دسست عمرا فأصبحت
حلائله منه أرامل ضيعا

TAB-FULL:v24p445/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r1.claim: The person who buries or debases the soul fails in seeking its good: God abandons it from guidance until it sins and disobeys.
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r1.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، {وقد خاب من دساها} [الشمس: 10] يقول: وقد خاب من دسى الله نفسه فأضله

TAB-FULL:v24p445/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r2.claim: The form dussāhā derives from doubled d-s-s with one sin changed to yāʾ, a sound change also seen in Arabic poetry.
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r2.anchor: والعرب تفعل ذلك كثيرا، فتبدل في الحرف المشدد بعض حروفه، ياء أحيانا، وواوا أحيانا؛ ومنه قول الآخر

TAB-FULL:v24p445/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God has debased the soul and led it astray.
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r3.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، {وقد خاب من دساها} [الشمس: 10] يقول: وقد خاب من دسى الله نفسه فأضله

TAB-FULL:v24p445/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r4.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbās report glosses it as the soul's denial.
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r4.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس: {وقد خاب من دساها} [الشمس: 10] يعني: تكذيبها

TAB-FULL:v24p445/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r5.speaker: مجاهد، سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r5.claim: Mujāhid and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr differ between saying God caused the soul to go astray and to be led astray.
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، {وقد خاب من دساها} [الشمس: 10] قال أحدهما: أغواها، وقال الآخر: أضلها

TAB-FULL:v24p445/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r6.claim: Qatāda says God made the soul sinful and wicked.
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {وقد خاب من دساها} [الشمس: 10] قال: أثمها وأفجرها

TAB-FULL:v24p445/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd also says the person fails when God debases the soul.
TAB-FULL:v24p445/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وقد خاب} [الشمس: 10] يقول: وقد خاب من دسى الله نفسه

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r7.claim: Success means attaining one’s goal and failure its opposite. Tazkiya evokes blessed plant-growth, while tadsiya means covertly inserting or corrupting something, here deforming the soul’s proper growth.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r7.anchor: والتزكية إنماؤه كذلك، والتدسي - وهو من الدس بقلب إحدى السينين ياء - إدخال الشيء في الشيء بضرب من الإخفاء

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r8.claim: These verses answer the oath and describe reform or corruption of the soul: innate recognition of piety makes submission to God natural, and taqwā cultivates it and supplies its lasting provision.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r8.anchor: والتعبير بالتزكية والتدسي عن إصلاح النفس وإفسادها مبتن على ما يدل عليه قوله { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها }

TABATABAI:91:11-15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r1.claim: Taqwā is the best provision for the soul’s lasting life, as the Qurʾān tells people to provision themselves with piety.
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r1.anchor: وتزودوا فإن خير الزاد التقوى واتقون يا أولي الألباب

ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r4.claim: Dassa means God made the soul low and base; the root form is dassasah, with one repeated consonant changed to yāʾ when like letters accumulate.
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r4.anchor: والأصل دسسها، ولكن الحروف إذا اجتمعت من لفظ واحد أبدل من أحدها ياء.

ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r5.claim: An anonymous poetic line, تقضي البازي إذا البازي كسر, illustrates the same consonant pattern, with taqaḍḍa intended.
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r5.anchor:
تقضي البازي إذا البازي كسر
قالوا معناه تقضض.

TABRISI:91:14/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14/r8.claim: Dassa is the opposite of zakā; the doubled root is softened by replacing one sīn, like other Arabic forms that avoid gemination.
TABRISI:91:14/r8.anchor: يقال دسا فلان يدسو دسوا فهو داس نقيض زكا

TABRISI:91:14/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14/r9.claim: The word may originally have had two sīns, one replaced by yāʾ to avoid doubling; the poet's taqaḍḍā illustrates the process.
TABRISI:91:14/r9.anchor: وقيل: إن أصل دسا دسس فأبدل من أحد السينين ياء

THALABI:v10p213/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p213/r2.claim: The soul fails when God abandons, forsakes, lowers, and conceals it as it commits sins and acts wickedly.
THALABI:v10p213/r2.anchor: خاب خسرت نفس من دساها دسسها الله فأهملها وخذلها ووضع منها

THALABI:v10p213/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p213/r3.claim: Arabic may alter a letter in a doubled consonant into yāʾ or wāw, as in the forms he cites.
THALABI:v10p213/r3.anchor: والعرب تفعل هذا كثير فيبدل في الحرف المشدد بعض حروفه ياء أو واو

THALABI:v10p213/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
THALABI:v10p213/r5.claim: One glosses its ruin as leading it astray, and the other as misguiding it.
THALABI:v10p213/r5.anchor: وقد خاب من دساها قال أحدهما: أغواها، وقال الآخر: أضلها

THALABI:v10p213/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r6.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p213/r6.claim: He glosses the phrase as making the soul sinful and wicked.

THALABI:v10p213/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p213/r7.claim: He glosses the phrase as nullifying and destroying the soul.

THALABI:v10p213/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
THALABI:v10p213/r8.claim: A soul succeeds when God purifies it and fails when God corrupts it.
THALABI:v10p213/r8.anchor: قد أفلحت نفس زكاها الله، وخابت نفس أفسدها الله عز وجل

THALABI:v10p213/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p213/r9.claim: A person may purify and reform the soul by making it obey God, or ruin it by leading it into disobedience.
THALABI:v10p213/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه قد أفلح من زكى نفسه فأصلحها وحملها على طاعة الله

THALABI:v10p213/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p213/r10.claim: On reciting the verse, the Prophet paused to ask God to grant his soul piety and purify it, since God is its guardian and best purifier.
THALABI:v10p213/r10.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ هذه الآية: قد أفلح من زكاها وقف ثم قال: «اللهم آت نفسي تقواها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r1.claim: The failed soul is one God has led astray, ruined, made sinful, and rendered immoral; these are their varied glosses of “dassaha.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r1.anchor: خابت، وخسرت نفس أضلها الله، وأغواها، وأبطلها، وأهلكها،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r2.speaker: الفراء، أبو عبيدة، أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r2.claim: “Dassaha” derives from concealment, originally with doubled s; one s shifted to y, as in the listed forms, and al-Farra gives further analogues such as dinar and diwan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r2.anchor: وهو إخفاء الشيء في الشيء، فأبدلت من إحدى السينات (¬7) "ياء"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r3.claim: The word can mean that God made the soul low and wretched.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معنى دساها: جعلها قليلة خسيسة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r4.claim: Here “dassaha” means He obscured, forsook, and hid the soul’s standing instead of making its obedience and good works manifest.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r4.anchor: ومعنى "دساها" هاهنا: أخملها (¬1)، وخذلها، وأخفى محلها، ولم يشهر مكانا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r7.speaker: عائشة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r7.claim: Aisha reports that she awoke one night to hear the Prophet pray that God grant his soul reverence and purify it, as its guardian and master.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p57/r7.anchor: الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- وهو يقول: "رب أعط نفسي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64/r1.claim: An alternative gloss describes someone who conceals himself among the righteous while inwardly differing from them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64/r1.anchor: معناه: من دس نفسه مع الصالحين، وليس هو منهم (¬1)، وهو

WAHIDI-QT:91:10/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:91:10/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:91:10/r1.claim: The failed soul is made low and base until it acts wickedly; its verb can mean concealing, lowering, burdening, or abandoning it.
WAHIDI-QT:91:10/r1.anchor: { وقد خاب من دساها } جعلها الله ذليلة خسيسة حتى عملت بالفجور ومعنى دساها أخفى محلها ووضع منها وأحملها وخذلها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r2.claim: The failed soul is made low and vile until it commits wickedness; the verb also suggests concealing, lowering, burdening, and abandoning it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r2.anchor: جعلها الله ذليلة خسيسة حتى عملت بالفجور، ومعنى دساها: أخفى محلها

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r15.claim: The one who corrupts and buries a soul in sin, or the degraded soul God consigns to ruin, fails and ends in hopeless loss and regret.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r15.anchor: tedsiye eden kimse de, yani korumayıp fücur ile tereddî ettirerek gömen dessas kimseler

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r16.claim: Most commentators take these two statements as the oath's answer; the lam of laqad is omitted because the oath is long, and the pair summarizes the surah's purpose.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r16.anchor: Ekser müfessirînin beyânına göre kasemlerin cevâbı bu iki cümledir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r9.claim: The same interpretive issue applies to the one who corrupts or buries the soul.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r10.claim: Tedsiyah is the opposite of purification: it can mean stunting or hiding, leading astray by deceit, corrupting, or burying something out of sight.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r10.anchor: bir şey neşv ü nemâ bulmayıp bodur ve cılız kalmak ve gizlenmek mânalarınadır.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r11.claim: Some derive the word instead from dess, with a geminated consonant altered to a weak letter in the past-tense form; dess and dissisa mean burying or concealing under something.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r12.claim: The source links Turkish desise to dissisa and notes desis can name persistent armpit odor, a spy, or roast meat buried in ashes, while dessas is a venomous snake.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r13.claim: The word thus conveys repeated deceit, spoiling something through guile, covering it over, and burying it.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r13.anchor: çok dess ve desîse yapmak, bir şeyi desîse ile bozup fenalaştırmak ve pek örtüp gizlemek, gömmek mânalarını ifade eder.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r14.speaker: الشاعر
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r14.claim: A poet says the addressee ruined and buried Amr, leaving his wives widowed; the verse illustrates tedsiyah as ruin and burial.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r14.anchor: وَأَنْتَ الَّذِي دَسَّسْتَ عَمْرًا فَأَصْبَحَتْ حَلَاَئِلُهُ مِنْهُ أَرَامِلَ ضُيَّعَا

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r15.claim: Burying the soul means failing to cultivate virtues and letting sin, vile bodily aims, ostentation, and dark feelings bury its divine light, ending in hell and loss.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r15.anchor: nefsi tedsiye rûhu fezâil ile tezkiye etmeyip fısk u fücur ve kötü ahlâk ile fesâda vermek

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r16.claim: Purification and inspiration correspond to daylight and sky, while burial corresponds to night and earth; hiding God's breathed spirit is a great loss.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r16.anchor: İlhâm-ı ilâhî ile tezkiyenin, nûr-ı nehâr ve semâya, tedsiyenin zulmet-i leyl ile Arz’a

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Lisān
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r1.claim: The Lisān first makes dassā an antonym of zakā, ‘be impure’; another interpretation equates it with dassasa/dassa, ‘hide or insert,’ which Schulthess follows.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Lisān bietet s. v. d-s-y zunächst eine offensichtlich von 91:10 abgeleitete Deutung von dasā als Antonym von zakā („unrein sein“)

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r2.claim: The ‘hide or insert’ derivation gives little sense in context and yields Schulthess’s translation ‘loses who hides it [the soul].’
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Inhaltlich wenig Sinn ergibt die Erklärung von dassā als Variante zu dassasa = dassa, „verbergen“ oder „hineinstecken“

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r3.claim: The Lisān’s independent poetic example uses dassā to mean ruin or corrupt; this is preferable because it does not derive the sense solely from the Quran or reduce it to an antonym of zakkā.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:10:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Für diese Erklärung spricht insbesondere, dass sie auf einer koranunabhängigen Belegstelle zu beruhen scheint

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.claim: The oath’s list of opposing created phenomena moves into morality in verses 7–8 and ends with a contrastive oath naming the opposed outcomes of those moral choices.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die Liste gegensätzlicher Schöpfungsphänomene, die in V. 7.8 in den Bereich des Moralischen übergeht, endet schließlich mit einer ebenfalls kontrastiv gegliederte Schwuraussage

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r2.claim: The feminine suffix -hā in verses 9–10 refers syntactically back to the soul in verse 7.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r2.anchor: Der enge sachliche Zusammenhang der Schwuraussage mit dem letzten Schwurelement, der Seele, zeigt sich dabei auch syntaktisch in dem pronominalen Rückbezug des femininen Suffixes -hā auf die nafs aus V. 7.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r3.claim: Although other early suras frame conduct and outcome eschatologically, this sura does not explicitly mention afterlife recompense; ashqā in verse 12 may carry such connotations.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r3.anchor: die vorliegende Sure nicht ausdrücklich auf eine jenseitige Vergeltung; allerdings dürfte der Gebrauch des Ausdrucks ʾašqā in V. 12 eschatologische Konnotationen transportiert haben

ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.claim: The preceding surah ended with the people of the right and left; this one summarizes the two groups in the successful purifier and failed corrupter, and its inspiration verse can explain the two paths in the previous surah.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.anchor: ولما ختم سبحانه السورة المتقدمة بذكر أصحاب الميمنة وأصحاب المشأمة أعاد جل شأنه في هذه السورة الفريقين على سبيل الفذلكة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r1.claim: Repeating قد emphasizes certainty and signals that the oath attaches to this assertion as well.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r1.anchor: وتكرير قد لأبراز الأعتناء بتحقيق مضمونه والإيذان بتعلق القسم به أصالة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r2.claim: تدسّى derives from doubled دسس, with the third identical consonant replaced by ي and then ألف; the root conveys intensified concealment, as in the poet's line about burying ʿAmr.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r2.anchor: وأصل دسى دسس فأبدل من ثالث التماثلات ياء ثم أبدلت ألفا لتحركها وانفتاح ما قبلها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses purification as growth and elevation, and concealment as diminishment and hiding: piety raises the soul in knowledge and action, while sin hides and diminishes it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r3.anchor: وفي الكشاف التزكية الإنماء والإعلاء والتدسية النقص والإخفاء أي لقد فاز بكل مطلوب ونجا من كل مكروه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes purification cleansing the soul from material stain and concealment hiding or entangling it in that matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r4.anchor: وجوز أن تفسر التزكية بالتطهير من دنس الهيولي والتدسية بالإخفاء فيه والتلوث به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r5.claim: The oath and paired promise and warning display God's knowledge, necessary existence, perfect attributes, and abundant gracious gifts to His servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r5.anchor: ففي الوعد والوعيد المذكورين مع إقسامه تعالى عليهما بما أقسم به مما يدل على العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r6.claim: A poetic line uses دسّ in the sense of hiding or burying someone in earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر ودسست عمرا في التراب فأصبحت حلائله منه أرامل ضيعا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the purification statements as a parenthesis and makes the oath's omitted answer a threat to destroy Meccan disbelievers as Thamūd were destroyed for rejecting Ṣāliḥ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري قوله تعالى قد أفلح الخ تابعا لقوله تعالى فألهمها الخ على سبيل الأستطراد وأبى أن يكون جواب القسم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.claim: Alusi objects that omitting the laam is far more common and less cumbersome than omitting an entire clause; purification is itself a central aim, not merely a practical-intellect concern or disposable preliminary.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.anchor: وتعقب بأن حذف اللام كثير لاسيما مع الطول وهو أسهل من حذف الجملة بتمامها وقد ذكره في قد أفلح المؤمنون

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r7.claim: The decree does not erase a role for human capacity and choice; assigning purification and concealment to people requires only their involvement, not that they independently create their acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r7.anchor: ولا يقتضي ذلك أن لا يكون لقدرة العبد واختياره مدخل في الفجور والتقوى بالكلية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r8.claim: Grammatical attribution to a person establishes involvement, not independent creation or autonomous power to choose and produce either state.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r8.anchor: لأن الإسناد يقتضي قيام المسند ويكفي فيه المدخلية المذكورة ولا يتوقف صحة الإسناد حقيقة إلى العبد على كون فعله الإيجاد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the successful person as one whose soul God purifies and guides, and the failed one as one whose soul God corrupts and misguides.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.anchor: قال في ذلك يقول الله تعالى قد أفلح من زكى الله تعالى نفسه فهداه وقد خاب من دسى الله تعالى نفسه فأضله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.speaker: صاحب الانتصاف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.claim: Some commentators and Ṣāḥib al-Intiṣāf prefer God as the subject of both verbs, citing these reports, consistent subjects throughout the oath, and the parallel passive-reflexive تزكى.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.anchor: ولهذه الأخبار ونحوها قال بعضهم أن ذلك هو المرجح ورجحه صاحب الانتصاف بأن الضمائر في السماء وما بناها الخ تكون عليه متسقة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.claim: Alusi says the human subject is still the first sense to occur to the mind, and the reports do not decisively establish the alternative; they do refute al-Zamakhsharī's charge that this is Sunnī reversal of the Qadarite position.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.anchor: ومع هذا كله لا ينبغي أن ينكر أن المعنى هو السابق إلى الذهن وما ذكر من الأخبار ليس نصا في تعيين المعنى الآخر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r2.claim: The soul God misleads and corrupts is ruined.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r2.anchor: أي خابت وخسرت نفس أضلها الله فأفسدها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan instead makes the person the subject: one succeeds by purifying and directing the soul to obedience, and loses by ruining it through sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه قد أفلح من زكى نفسه فأصلحها وحملها على طاعة الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r4.claim: Dassa derives from repeated hiding (dassasa); the second sīn becomes yāʾ, and the sense is to abase or conceal the soul through unbelief and disobedience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r4.anchor: أصله: دسسها من التدسيس، وهو إخفاء الشيء، فأبدلت السين الثانية ياء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r5.claim: Zayd b. Arqam reports that the Prophet sought refuge from incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, worry, and grave punishment, asking God to grant and purify the soul’s piety and protect from other spiritual failings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r5.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال: لا أقول لكم إلا ما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنا: "اللهم إني أعوذ بك

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r3.claim: The loser diminishes and conceals the soul through ignorance and disobedience; the form دسّى contracts from دسس, like تقضى from تقضض.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r3.anchor: نقصها وأخفاها بالجهالة والفسوق، وأصل دسى دسس كتقضي وتقضض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r3.claim: The one who corrupts the soul loses the promised afterlife reward and ruins it through corrupt beliefs, deeds, intentions, and states.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r3.anchor: أي إغواها إغواء عظيما وأفسدها ودنس محياها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r4.claim: Biqāʿī derives dassā from d-s-s and develops a spiritual allegory: the sun is prophethood, its dawn the message, its moon sainthood, daylight gnosis, and night estrangement from God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r4.anchor: فالتزكية أن يحرص الإنسان على شمسه أن لا تكسف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r5.claim: In this allegory, the sky represents dignity above passions and satanic steps, while the earth represents humility and bringing benefits to believers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r5.anchor: ونظير السماء العزة والترفع عن الشهوات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r6.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī are quoted as saying that if scholars are not God's friends, then God has no friend.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r6.anchor: إن لم تكن العلماء أولياء الله فليس الله ولي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r7.claim: A cited poem says generous people's connection is easy for the needy, while their station is difficult for warriors, contrasting visible generosity with hidden miserliness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r7.anchor: قوم على المحتاج سهل وصلهم ومقامهم وعر على الفرسان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r8.claim: The warning follows the preceding Sūrat al-Balad and the earlier mention of rebellion to spur purification.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r8.anchor: ولما كان السياق للترهيب بما دلت عليه سورة البلد وتقديم الفجور هنا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r1.claim: The following Sūrat al-Layl shares al-Shams's theme: God has complete power and choice, shown by people's different paths despite shared aims in sensual pleasures and comfort.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r2.claim: Night's darkness and sleep, the sibling of death, frustrate many human desires and bring about opposing outcomes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r2.anchor: ليل نفسه دال على ذلك لأنه على غير مراد النفس بما فيه من الظلام

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.claim: He says purification means improving the soul, concealment means leading it astray, Thamud denied through disobedience, and God does not fear their aftermath.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.anchor: قال: عرفها شقاءها {قد أفلح من زكاها} قال: أصلحها {وقد خاب من دساها} قال: أغواها

DURR-FULL:v8p529/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r7.claim: Failure is for the one who stains the soul with sin and immorality.

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r12.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r12.claim: He says God purifies the soul of the successful and darkens the soul of the failed.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r12.anchor: عن الكلبي {قد أفلح من زكاها} الآية قال: أفلح من زكاه الله وخاب من دساه الله

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r13.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r13.claim: He says success is purifying and reforming oneself, while failure is ruining and misleading oneself.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r13.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية: قد أفلح من زكى نفسه وأصلحها وخاب من أهلكها وأضلها

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r14.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r14.claim: He connects purifying the soul to righteous work and concealing it to evil work.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r14.anchor: عن الربيع في الآية يقول: أفلح من زكى نفسه بالعمل الصالح وخاب من دس نفسه بالعمل السيء

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r15.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r15.claim: He glosses ‘dassaha’ as losing the soul.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r15.anchor: عن عكرمة من {دساها} قال: من خسرها

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r16.claim: He says God purifies the successful soul and darkens and misguides the failed one.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r16.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {قد أفلح من زكاها} يقول: قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

DURR-FULL:v8p531/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r1.claim: He glosses concealment of the soul as deceiving it.
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وقد خاب من دساها} يعني: مكر بها

DURR-FULL:v8p531/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says a soul prospers when God purifies it and fails when God deprives it of every good.
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: {قد أفلح من زكاها} الآية

ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r1.claim: Tadsiyah means concealment, from d-s-s; the third doubled consonant is replaced by a weak letter, as in the cited form naqaṣ.

ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r2.claim: An unnamed poet's line using dassasta, and another line about burying ʿAmr, support the sense of concealment.
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر : وأنت الذي دسست عمراً فأصبحت

ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r3.claim: One may conceal oneself among righteous people through hypocrisy without belonging to them.
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r3.anchor: وقال تعالى : { دساها } في أهل الخير بالرياء وليس منهم

ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r4.claim: Mentioning piety is followed by the success of the one who purifies the soul; mentioning concealment is followed by the people of Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN:91:10/r4.anchor: ولما قال : { وقد خاب من دساها } ،   أعقبه بأهل الجنة

ALUSI:91:9/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r2.claim: The subject of each verb is the pronoun referring to من, while the suffix refers to the soul.
ALUSI:91:9/r2.anchor: وفاعل زكاها ضمير من والضمير المنصوب للنفس وكذا في قوله تعالى

ALUSI:91:9/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r3.claim: Repeating قد emphasizes the certainty of the second statement and signals that the oath directly concerns it as well.
ALUSI:91:9/r3.anchor: وتكرير قد فيه لإبراز الاعتناء بتحقيق مضمونه والإيذان بتعلق القسم به أصالة

ALUSI:91:9/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r4.claim: Tazkiya means growth, while tadsiyah means concealment.

ALUSI:91:9/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r5.claim: The form dassā derives from dassasa: one of three identical consonants became yāʾ, then alif because it was vowelled after fatḥa.
ALUSI:91:9/r5.anchor: وأصل دسى دسس فأبدل من ثالث التماثلات ياء ثم أبدلت ألفاً لتحركها وانفتاح ما قبلها

ALUSI:91:9/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:91:9/r6.claim: Some grammarians generalize the change as replacement by a weak letter, comparing it with تقضض becoming تقضي; dass is an intensive form of concealment.
ALUSI:91:9/r6.anchor: وأطلق بعضهم فقال ابدل من ذلك حرف علة كما قالوافي تقضض تقضي ودسس مبالغة في دس بمعنى أخفى

ALUSI:91:9/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r7.speaker: الشاعر
