ALUSI:91:9/r7.claim: An unnamed poet’s line about burying ʿAmr in the earth illustrates the concealment sense of the root.
ALUSI:91:9/r7.anchor:
قال الشاعر
: ودسست عمراً في التراب فأصبحت ***

ALUSI:91:9/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r8.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI:91:9/r8.claim: Al-Kashshāf glosses tazkiya as growth and elevation, and tadsiyah as diminution and concealment.
ALUSI:91:9/r8.anchor: التزكية الإنماء والإعلاء والتدسية النقص والإخفاء

ALUSI:91:9/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r9.claim: The successful person grows and elevates the soul through taqwā in knowledge and action; the loser diminishes and hides it through sin, ignorance and transgression.
ALUSI:91:9/r9.anchor: أي لقد فاز بكل مطلوب ونجا من كل مكروه من أنمى نفسه وأعلاها بالتقوى علماً وعملاً

ALUSI:91:9/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r10.claim: Another reading takes tazkiya as purification from the dross of matter and tadsiyah as hiding in and becoming polluted by it.
ALUSI:91:9/r10.anchor: وجوز أن تفسر التزكية بالتطهير من دنس الهيولى والتدسية بالإخفاء فيه والتلوث به

ALUSI:91:9/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r11.claim: The promised success and threatened loss, sworn to by these signs, attest to God’s knowledge, necessary existence and perfect attributes, and display His beneficence toward servants.
ALUSI:91:9/r11.anchor: ففي الوعد والوعيد المذكورين مع إقسامه تعالى عليهما بما أقسم به مما يدل على العلم بوجوده تعالى ووجوب ذاته

ALUSI:91:10/r9.speaker: author

ALUSI:91:10/r9.anchor: أي لقد فاز بكل مطلوب ونجا من كل مكروه من أنمى نفسه وأعلاها بالتقوى علماً وعملاً

BAGHAWI:91:10/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:10/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:91:10/r1.claim: The soul God misleads and corrupts has failed and lost.
BAGHAWI:91:10/r1.anchor: أي خابت وخسرت نفس أضلها الله فأفسدها

BAGHAWI:91:10/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:10/r2.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI:91:10/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the successful person purifies and directs himself to obedience, while the failed person ruins and misleads himself toward sin; this reading makes the soul the agent of the verbs.
BAGHAWI:91:10/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن : معناه قد أفلح من زكى نفسه فأصلحها وحملها على طاعة الله عز وجل

BAGHAWI:91:10/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:10/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:91:10/r3.claim: Dassa-ha derives from the form dassasaha, from tad sīs, concealment; the second sīn changed to yāʾ. Here it means to debase the soul and hide its standing through disbelief and sin.
BAGHAWI:91:10/r3.anchor: { دساها } أصله : دسسها من التدسيس ، وهو إخفاء الشيء ، فأبدلت السين الثانية ياء

BAGHAWI:91:10/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:10/r4.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
BAGHAWI:91:10/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam transmits the Prophet's prayer seeking refuge from incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, senility, and the grave's punishment; it asks God to grant and purify the soul's piety, then seeks refuge from useless knowledge, an unsated soul, an unhumble heart, and unanswered supplication.
BAGHAWI:91:10/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال : " لا أقول لكم إلا ما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنا : اللهم إني أعوذ بك

BAYDAWI:91:10/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:10/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:10/r1.claim: The loser is one who diminishes and conceals the soul through ignorance and sinfulness.
BAYDAWI:91:10/r1.anchor: وقد خاب من دساها نقصها وأخفاها بالجهالة والفسوق

BAYDAWI:91:10/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:10/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:10/r2.claim: Dassa is originally dasasa, contracted like taqaḍḍā from taqaḍḍaḍa.

BIQAI:91:10/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:10/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:10/r1.claim: The loser is deprived of the afterlife prepared for others, loses, and labors in vain; corrupting the soul means misleading, defiling, degrading, and ruining it through corrupt beliefs, acts, intentions, and states.
BIQAI:91:10/r1.anchor: أي حرم مراده مما أعد لغيره في الدار الآخرة وخسر وكان سعيه باطلاً

BIQAI:91:10/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:10/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:10/r2.claim: The underlying form of dassā is dassasa (دسس).

BIQAI:91:10/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:10/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:10/r3.claim: He compares purification to keeping the sun, moon, day, and night clear, then maps them inwardly: sun is prophecy, its brightness/message is the mission, moon is sainthood, day is gnosis, and night is a soul unquiet in God's remembrance and revelation.
BIQAI:91:10/r3.anchor: فنظير الشمس هي النبوة لأنها كلها ضياء باهر وصفاء قاهر ،   وضحاها الرسالة وقمرها الولاية ،   والنهار هو العرفان

BIQAI:91:10/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:10/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:10/r4.claim: He likens the sky to dignity above desire and satanic promptings, and earth to humility before God, His Messenger, and believers, bringing them benefits; corruption is the opposite.
BIQAI:91:10/r4.anchor: ونظير السماء العزة والترفع عن الشهوات وعن خطوات الشياطين من الإنس والجن ،   والأرض نظيرها التواضع لحق الله

BIQAI:91:10/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:10/r5.speaker: العلماء العاملون
BIQAI:91:10/r5.claim: Biqāʿī calls scholars who act on their knowledge God's saints and cites the saying attributed to Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī that, otherwise, God would have no saint; al-Khaṭīb transmitted it.
BIQAI:91:10/r5.anchor: قال الإمامان أبو حنيفة والشافعي رضي الله عنهما : إن لم تكن العلماء أولياء الله

BIQAI:91:10/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:10/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:10/r6.claim: Wrongdoers debase and hide themselves like misers concealed in valley bottoms; generous people live openly on heights and light fires for visitors, as the anonymous verse illustrates.
BIQAI:91:10/r6.anchor: كما أن اللئام ينزلون بطون الأودية ومقاطعها بحيث تخفى أماكنهم على الطارقين ،   والأجواد ينزلون الروابي

DURR:91:9/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r1.speaker: الكلبي
DURR:91:9/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says success is for the soul God purifies and failure for the soul God debases.
DURR:91:9/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي { قد أفلح من زكاها } الآية ، قال : أفلح من زكاه الله وخاب من دساه الله .

DURR:91:9/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR:91:9/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the successful person purifies and reforms the soul, while the loser destroys and misguides it.
DURR:91:9/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية : قد أفلح من زكى نفسه وأصلحها ، وخاب من أهلكها وأضلها .

DURR:91:9/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r3.speaker: الربيع
DURR:91:9/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the soul is purified through righteous deeds and debased through evil deeds.
DURR:91:9/r3.anchor: عن الربيع في الآية ، يقول : أفلح من زكى نفسه بالعمل الصالح ، وخاب من دس نفسه بالعمل السيئ .

DURR:91:9/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:91:9/r4.claim: Ikrimah explains “dassāhā” as losing the soul.
DURR:91:9/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة من { دساها } قال : من خسرها .

DURR:91:9/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:91:9/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God purifies the successful soul and hides or debases the failed one, leading it astray; he adds that the one described does not fear anyone who follows him.
DURR:91:9/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { قد أفلح من زكاها } يقول : قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

DURR:91:9/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:91:9/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses “dassāhā” as having plotted or schemed against the soul.
DURR:91:9/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس { وقد خاب من دساها } يعني : مكر بها .

DURR:91:9/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:91:9/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through al-Dahhak attributes to the Prophet the saying that the soul God purifies succeeds, while the soul He deprives of all good fails.
DURR:91:9/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : { قد أفلح من زكاها }

DURR:91:10/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r1.speaker: الكلبي
DURR:91:10/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says success is for the soul God purifies and failure for the soul God debases.
DURR:91:10/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي { قد أفلح من زكاها } الآية ، قال : أفلح من زكاه الله وخاب من دساه الله .

DURR:91:10/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR:91:10/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the successful person purifies and reforms the soul, while the loser destroys and misguides it.
DURR:91:10/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية : قد أفلح من زكى نفسه وأصلحها ، وخاب من أهلكها وأضلها .

DURR:91:10/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r3.speaker: الربيع
DURR:91:10/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the soul is purified through righteous deeds and debased through evil deeds.
DURR:91:10/r3.anchor: عن الربيع في الآية ، يقول : أفلح من زكى نفسه بالعمل الصالح ، وخاب من دس نفسه بالعمل السيئ .

DURR:91:10/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:91:10/r4.claim: Ikrimah explains “dassāhā” as losing the soul.
DURR:91:10/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة من { دساها } قال : من خسرها .

DURR:91:10/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:91:10/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God purifies the successful soul and hides or debases the failed one, leading it astray; he adds that the one described does not fear anyone who follows him.
DURR:91:10/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { قد أفلح من زكاها } يقول : قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

DURR:91:10/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:91:10/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses “dassāhā” as having plotted or schemed against the soul.
DURR:91:10/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس { وقد خاب من دساها } يعني : مكر بها .

DURR:91:10/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:91:10/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through al-Dahhak attributes to the Prophet the saying that the soul God purifies succeeds, while the soul He deprives of all good fails.
DURR:91:10/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : { قد أفلح من زكاها }

IBNATIYYA:91:10/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r1.claim: Dassāhā means to conceal and debase the soul, diminishing its worth through sins and withholding what is due.
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r1.anchor: و { دساها } معناه : أخفاها وحقرها أي وصغر قدرها بالمعاصي والبخل بما يجب

IBNATIYYA:91:10/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r2.claim: The verb is used as dasā-yadsū or with doubled sīn as dassā-yudassī; its root form is d-s-s.
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r2.anchor: يقال دسا يدسو ودسّى بشد السين يدسي وأصله دسس

IBNATIYYA:91:10/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r3.claim: The cited poem uses the related form dasastu for burying or corrupting someone, supporting the sense of concealment and ruin.

IBNATIYYA:91:10/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r4.claim: When reciting this passage, the Prophet prayed for his soul to receive piety and purification, saying God is its best purifier and its guardian.
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r4.anchor: ويروى أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ هذه الآية قال : «اللهم آت نفسي تقواها وزكّها أنت خير من زكاها أنت وليها ومولاها

IBNATIYYA:91:10/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r5.claim: The Prophetic supplication supports taking God as the one who purifies the soul in the preceding verse.
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r5.anchor: هذا الحديث يقوي أن المزكي هو الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:91:10/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r6.speaker: ثعلب
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r6.claim: Thaʿlab takes the verse to describe someone who mingles with the righteous through ostentation but does not truly belong among them.
IBNATIYYA:91:10/r6.anchor: وقال ثعلب معنى الآية { وقد خاب من دساها } في أهل الخير بالرياء وليس منهم في حقيقته

MAWARDI:91:10/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:10/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:91:10/r1.claim: One view makes God the agent who stifles the soul in accordance with His decree; the other makes the person the agent who stifles their own soul.
MAWARDI:91:10/r1.anchor: أحدهما : على ما قضى وقد خاب من دسّى الله نفسه . الثاني : من دسّى نفسه

MAWARDI:91:10/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:10/r2.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI:91:10/r2.claim: Dassāhā means led it astray: the person hid themself in sins; an unattributed poet’s line uses the same verb of hiding or ruining ʿAmr.
MAWARDI:91:10/r2.anchor: أحدها : أغواها وأضلها ، قاله مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير ، لأنه دسّى نفسه في المعاصي ، ومنه قول الشاعر

MAWARDI:91:10/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:10/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:91:10/r3.claim: Dassāhā refers to the soul’s sin and wickedness.

MAWARDI:91:10/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:10/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:91:10/r5.claim: Dassāhā means denied or lied about it.

MAWARDI:91:10/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:10/r7.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:91:10/r7.claim: Dassāhā means kept it away from good.
MAWARDI:91:10/r7.anchor: السادس : جنبها في الخير ، وهذا قول الضحاك

MAWARDI:91:10/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:10/r8.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI:91:10/r8.claim: Dassāhā means concealed and diminished it through miserliness.
MAWARDI:91:10/r8.anchor: السابع : أخفاها وأخملها بالبخل ، حكاه ابن عيسى

NASAFI:91:10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:10/r1.claim: The one whose soul God misleads fails.
NASAFI:91:10/r1.anchor: { وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دساها } أغواها الله

NASAFI:91:10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:10/r2.speaker: عكرمة
NASAFI:91:10/r2.claim: Ikrima says the soul purified by God prospers and the soul misled by God fails.
NASAFI:91:10/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة : أفلحت نفس زكاها الله وخابت نفس أغواها الله

NASAFI:91:10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:10/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:10/r3.claim: Alternatively, purifying and concealing the soul may be acts of the servant.
NASAFI:91:10/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون التدسية والتطهير فعل العبد

NASAFI:91:10/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:10/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:10/r4.claim: Concealment is diminution and hiding through wickedness; “dassā” derives from “dassasa,” with yāʾ replacing a doubled sīn.
NASAFI:91:10/r4.anchor: والتدسية : النقص والإخفاء بالفجور وأصل دسّى دسس ، والياء بدل من السين المكررة

QURTUBI:91:10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:10/r1.claim: The soul is ruined when God buries it in disobedience.
QURTUBI:91:10/r1.anchor: أي خسرت نفس دسها الله عز وجل بالمعصية

QURTUBI:91:10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:91:10/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as a soul God led astray and caused to deviate.
QURTUBI:91:10/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : خابت نفس أضلها وأغواها

QURTUBI:91:10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r3.speaker: قتادة وغيره
QURTUBI:91:10/r3.claim: Qatāda and others contrast the successful person who purifies the soul through obedience and good works with one who buries it in sins.
QURTUBI:91:10/r3.anchor: وقيل : أفلح من زكى نفسه بطاعة الله ، وصالح الأعمال ، وخاب من دس نفسه في المعاصي . قاله قتادة وغيره

QURTUBI:91:10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:10/r4.claim: Zakāh fundamentally means growth and increase; the crop grows abundantly, and a judge's validation and praise elevate a witness.
QURTUBI:91:10/r4.anchor: وأصل الزكاة : النمو والزيادة ، ومنه زكا الزرع : إذا كثر ريعه

QURTUBI:91:10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:10/r5.claim: The one who does good and hastens to righteous works makes himself known and raises himself, like generous Arabs who camp high and light fires for travelers.
QURTUBI:91:10/r5.anchor: فمصطنع المعروف والمبادر إلى أعمال البر ، شهر نفسه ورفعها

QURTUBI:91:10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:10/r6.claim: Miserly Arabs hid in caves, outskirts, and valley bottoms; morally, they concealed and buried themselves, unlike those who elevate and purify themselves.
QURTUBI:91:10/r6.anchor: فأولئك علوا أنفسهم وزكوها ، وهؤلاء أخفوا أنفسهم ودسوها

QURTUBI:91:10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:10/r7.claim: A sinner is characteristically obscure and low in standing, with head bowed because of committing sins.
QURTUBI:91:10/r7.anchor: وكذا الفاجر أبدا خفي المكان ، زمر

QURTUBI:91:10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:10/r8.claim: An unattributed interpretation glosses d s y as leading astray; the cited poem uses it of luring and ruining ʿAmr.

QURTUBI:91:10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r9.speaker: أهل اللغة
QURTUBI:91:10/r9.claim: Linguists derive the form from dassasah, concealment, with the second s changed to y as in qaṣṣaytu from qaṣaṣtu; taqaḍḍu likewise becomes taqaḍḍī.
QURTUBI:91:10/r9.anchor: قال أهل اللغة : والأصل : دسسها ، من التدسيس ، وهو إخفاء الشيء

QURTUBI:91:10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:10/r10.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI:91:10/r10.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says it means hiding oneself among the righteous while not actually belonging to them.
QURTUBI:91:10/r10.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي : " وقد خاب من دساها " أي دس نفسه في جملة الصالحين

RAZI:91:10/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:10/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:91:10/r1.claim: Rāzī derives dassāhā from the doubled root d-s-s and tadīs, meaning to conceal one thing within another, with one s changed to yāʾ.

RAZI:91:10/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:10/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:91:10/r2.claim: He supports the morphology by comparing other forms whose original doubled consonants were simplified, including taqaḍḍaḍa, labibt, and mulabbab.

RAZI:91:10/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:10/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:91:10/r3.claim: The Muʿtazilites say the righteous make themselves visible, while the sinful hide; generous Arabs advertise their lodgings and fires, unlike misers who conceal their whereabouts.
RAZI:91:10/r3.anchor: أما المعتزلة فذكروا وجوها توافق قولهم

RAZI:91:10/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:10/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:91:10/r4.claim: One Muʿtazilite explanation is that the loser inserts himself among the righteous despite not belonging to them.
RAZI:91:10/r4.anchor: أي دس نفسه في جملة الصالحين وليس منهم

RAZI:91:10/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:10/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:91:10/r5.claim: Another explanation is that the person immerses himself in sins.

RAZI:91:10/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:10/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:91:10/r6.claim: Another explanation is that persistent sin and company with sinners plant wickedness in a person's soul.
RAZI:91:10/r6.anchor: وذلك بسبب مواظبته عليها ومجالسته مع أهلها

RAZI:91:10/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:10/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:91:10/r7.claim: Another explanation is that neglecting obedience for sins makes a person obscure, forsaken, and forgotten, like something concealed.
RAZI:91:10/r7.anchor: فصار كالشيء المدسوس في الاختفاء والخمول

RAZI:91:10/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:10/r8.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI:91:10/r8.claim: Rāzī's own school says the soul has failed and lost when God misguides it, makes it wicked, nullifies it, and destroys it.
RAZI:91:10/r8.anchor: نفس أضلها الله تعالى وأغواها وأفجرها

RAZI:91:10/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:10/r9.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:91:10/r9.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the oath by God's noblest creatures establishes the success of the purified and loss of the forsaken, so people do not suppose they purify or ruin themselves independently of prior decree.
RAZI:91:10/r9.anchor: الواحدي رحمه الله : فكأنه سبحانه أقسم

TAB:91:10/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:10/r1.speaker: author
TAB:91:10/r1.claim: The loser fails to attain the soul's reform: God debases it and withholds guidance, so it commits sins and abandons obedience.
TAB:91:10/r1.anchor: وقد خاب في طِلبته ،   فلم يُدرك ما طلب والتمس لنفسه من الصلاح مَنْ دسّاهَا يعني :  من دَسّس الله نفسه

TAB:91:10/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:10/r2.speaker: author
TAB:91:10/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī derives dassāhā from dassasahā, with one doubled s replaced by y; al-ʿAjjāj's poetic taqaḍḍā for taqaḍḍu illustrates the substitution.
TAB:91:10/r2.anchor: *** تَقَضّيَ الْبازِي إذا البازِي كَسَرْ *** يريد :  تَقَضّض

TAB:91:10/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:10/r3.speaker: author
TAB:91:10/r3.claim: Arabic also replaces a letter in a doubled consonant with another letter, as an unnamed poet's al-taẓannī witnesses for al-taẓannun.
TAB:91:10/r3.anchor: والعرب تفعل ذلك كثيرا ،   فتبدل في الحرف المشدّد بعضَ حروفه ،   ياء أحيانا ،   وواوا أحيانا ومنه قول الاَخر :  يَذْهَبُ بِي فِي الشّعْرِ كُلّ فَنّ

TAB:91:10/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:10/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:91:10/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the person has lost when God buries the soul and leads it astray.
TAB:91:10/r4.anchor: عن عليّ ،   عن ابن عباس وَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ دَسّاها يقول :  وقد خاب من دَسّى الله نُفسَه فأضلّه .

TAB:91:10/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:10/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:91:10/r5.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as the soul's denial.
TAB:91:10/r5.anchor: عن أبيه ،   عن ابن عباس :  وَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ دَسّاها يعني :  تكذيبها .

TAB:91:10/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:10/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:91:10/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the verb means that the soul was led astray.
TAB:91:10/r6.anchor: عن خَصِيف ،   عن مجاهد وَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ دَسّاها قال :  أضلها

TAB:91:10/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:10/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB:91:10/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the verb means that the soul was seduced or led into error.
TAB:91:10/r7.anchor: عن خَصِيف ،   عن مجاهد وَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ دَسّاها قال :  أضلها ،   وقال سعيد :  من أغواها .

TAB:91:10/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:10/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB:91:10/r8.claim: Qatāda explains the phrase as making the soul sinful and wicked.
TAB:91:10/r8.anchor: عن قتادة وَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ دَسّاها قال :  أثّمها وأفجرها .

TAB:91:10/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:10/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:91:10/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says the loser is one whose soul God has caused to sink or be debased.
TAB:91:10/r9.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  وَقَدْ خابَ يقول :  وقد خاب من دَسّى اللّهُ نَفسَه .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r5.claim: To bury the soul is to diminish and conceal it by abandoning good works and committing sins; the wicked hide themselves and lose dignity.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r5.anchor: وقد خاب من دساها، أي: نقصها وأخفاها بترك عمل البر، وبركوب المعاصي

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r6.claim: Dassa is derived from dassastu, with one doubled s converted to y, as in labibt/labayt and qasaytu from qasasstu.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r6.anchor: ودساها: من دسست، فقلبت إحدى السينات ياء، كما يقال: لببت، والأصل لبيت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r7.claim: Arab benefactors camped conspicuously on hills and lit night fires for visitors, while misers hid in recesses; their habits exemplify raising or burying the self.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r7.anchor: وكانت أجواد العرب تنزل الربا وأيفاع الأرض، لتشتهر أماكنها للمعتفين، وتوقد النيران في الليل للطارقين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r8.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r8.claim: An unnamed poet praises a conspicuous, spacious home that feeds visitors, illustrating the virtue of making oneself known to those seeking hospitality.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر : وبوأت بيتك في معلم ... رحيب المباءة والمسرح كفيت العفاة طلاب القرى

ALUSI:91:11/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:91:11/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes ‘successful is whoever purified it’ parenthetical after the inspiration clause, not the oath’s answer; he infers an omitted answer that God will destroy Meccan unbelievers for rejecting the Messenger as He destroyed Thamūd for rejecting Ṣāliḥ.
ALUSI:91:11/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري قوله تعالى : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ } الخ تابعاً لقوله تعالى : { فَأَلْهَمَهَا } الخ

ALUSI:91:11/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the objection that this requires omitting the oath’s lām and improperly emphasizing practical purification over the higher goal of certain belief.
ALUSI:91:11/r3.anchor: فقيل إن ذلك لما يلزم من حذف اللام وأنه لا يليق بالنظم المعجز أن يجعل أدنى الكمالين

ALUSI:91:11/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r4.claim: He replies that deleting the lām is common, especially after a long phrase, and is easier than deleting an entire sentence; al-Zamakhsharī himself accepts an omitted oath answer at 23:1.
ALUSI:91:11/r4.anchor: وقد ذكره في { قد أفلح المؤمنون } [ المرمنون : 1 ] فما حدا مما بدأ وأن التزكية

ALUSI:91:11/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r5.claim: Purification, understood as growth, is not confined to practical action and is itself an intended end, though even a prerequisite may appropriately receive emphasis.
ALUSI:91:11/r5.anchor: وأن التزكية مراداً بها الإنماء لا اختصاص لها وليست مقدمة بل مقصودة بالذات

ALUSI:91:11/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r10.claim: Divine decree does not erase all human agency: even if God ultimately creates the acts, the servant’s participation in purification or corruption suffices for the attribution to him; the text does not prove independent power to choose and create either course.
ALUSI:91:11/r10.anchor: ولا يقتضي ذلك أن لا يكون لقدرة العبد واختياره مدخل في الفجور والتقوى بالكلية

ALUSI:91:11/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:91:11/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the successful soul as one God purifies and guides, and the failed soul as one God corrupts and leads astray; this reading makes God the subject of the purification and corruption verbs.
ALUSI:91:11/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال في ذلك يقول الله تعالى

ALUSI:91:11/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r16.claim: Despite those reports, al-Ālūsī says the human-agent reading remains the more immediate sense; the reports do not conclusively establish the alternate subject, but refute al-Zamakhsharī’s charge that it is Sunni ‘inversion’ of the Qadari position.
ALUSI:91:11/r16.anchor: لا ينبغي أن ينكر أن المعنى السابق هو السابق إلى الذهن وما ذكر من الأخبار ليس نصاً في تعيين المعنى الآخر
